strengths: Novel information-theoretic framework for understanding PTQ optimality; rigorous analysis showing gap between GPTQ and IT limits with 0.255-bit guarantee
Strong empirical results achieving SOTA across 1-4 bit quantization rates on multiple models (Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3-8B, Llama-2-7B)
Comprehensive experimental analysis with detailed ablations demonstrating contribution of each component and per-layer diagnostics
Per-channel rate allocation inspired by waterfilling is well-motivated and shows consistent improvements over uniform allocation in GPTQ
Well-written paper with clear exposition of waterfilling intuition and detailed algorithmic descriptions (Algorithms 1-4)
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: theoretical analysis assumes iid Gaussian weights with a=1 but real LLM weights have structure and outliers; connection to actual performance not quantified

Algorithm combines 8+ distinct techniques with unclear individual importance; golden-section search per layer and adaptive mixing make it complex; initial hyperparameter choices appear ad-hoc (τ=10^-3 threshold)

Limited evaluation scope: no models larger than 8B parameters; weight-only quantization only; no hardware deployment results or end-to-end inference measurements; comparisons limited to weight-only methods
Dependency on external compression algorithms (Huffman/Zstd/LZMA) for final rate introduces deployment-time uncertainty; hardware support limited (Blackwell only)

Computational cost of quantization not reported (binary search, golden-section search, per-layer optimization); comparison with SOTA methods using end-to-end fine-tuning excluded; claim of 'no fine-tuning' misleading given per-layer calibration optimization

strengths: First rigorous information-theoretic analysis of LLM weight quantization with precisely characterized 0.255-bit gap to IT limit
Novel column-specific rate allocation principle inspired by classical waterfilling, well-motivated and theoretically justified
State-of-the-art empirical results across 5 model families (Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3-8B, Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-70B) and 1-4 bit quantization
Comprehensive practical algorithm with multiple well-designed components and extensive ablation studies demonstrating individual contributions
Exceptional experimental rigor with multiple evaluation datasets, zero-shot benchmarks, and detailed hyperparameter documentation enabling reproducibility
Honest discussion of limitations including scope, assumptions, and practical deployment challenges
weaknesses: Significant gap between theoretical assumptions and practice: theory assumes i.i.d. Gaussian weight rows (empirically only 70% match), analyzes single-row quantization despite practical use of large matrices, and doesn't account for all approximations in practical algorithm

Fundamental reliance on entropy coding for variable rates creates practical deployment concerns not adequately addressed: hardware support is future work, no throughput/latency benchmarks provided, actual deployment efficiency compared to fixed-rate methods unclear

Algorithm complexity obscures core contribution: many hyperparameters (δ, c, ϵ_qr, ϵ_aw, τ), model-specific tuning required (e.g., Qwen3-8B outlier handling, layer-16 phase transition), raises generalizability questions

Finetuning results conflate contributions: WaterSIC-FT shows 60% PPL reduction over base WaterSIC at 1 bit, suggesting either base algorithm underperforms or finetuning provides orthogonal gains unrelated to core contribution
Modest gains at practical bitrates: improvements concentrate at 1-2 bits where PPLs remain very high; at 4 bits (commonly used), gains are ~0.1 PPL over baselines

Limited scope of evaluation: dense models only (no sparse/MoE architectures), large distribution mismatch between WikiText-2 calibration and C4 evaluation, some baselines reproduced with different hyperparameters
Theoretical novelty is limited: main result follows straightforwardly from applying known IT results (waterfilling + Zamir et al. 2006), connection to GPTQ interesting but not deeply novel

Incomplete analysis of Gaussianity assumption: Figure 11 shows significant deviations for wq/wk matrices; no analysis of performance degradation for non-Gaussian weights or whether alternative distributions would improve results
